newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE TO BUILD NEW AIRPORT NEXT MONTH -PAPER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE TO BUILD NEW AIRPORT NEXT MONTH -PAPER.

text.p: Zimbabwe's cash-strapped government will from February start building a new international airport in Harare which has been in the pipeline since the mid-1980s, the official Herald newspaper reported on Thursday.

It said President Robert Mugabe would, on his 73rd birthday on February 21, lay the foundation stone for the Z$810 million (US$74 million) airport whose tender was won last year by Cyprus-based Air Harbour Technologies (AHT) amid much controversy.

The award of the tender to AHT drew widespread criticism from Western diplomats who alleged lack of transparency in the tender procedure after President Mugabe's cabinet suspended recommendations by the government tender board which had a French company, Aeroport de Paris, topping the contractors' list.
Zimbabwe's independent press criticised the award of the tender to AHT, which they said was represented locally by Mugabe's nephew Leo Mugabe.
Transport and Energy Minister Simon Moyo defended the government's choice, saying the AHT design fully met government requirements that it had to be functional and uniquely Zimbabwean.
Western donors subsequently said they were withholding aid for the new airport.

On Thursday, government officials were unavailable for comment on the financial arrangements for the project but the Herald reported that the finance ministry would next week finalise details of the financial package with foreign banks.
